alphas.nickname: Frazzini-Pedersen 2014 betting-against-beta
alphas.notes: Frazzini & Pedersen (2014) BAB. Price-only proxy: market return is the cross-sectional mean of daily per-stock returns (equal-weighted, not value-weighted as in the original). Beta is Cov(r_i, r_m) / Var(r_m) over a single 252-day window (paper uses separate 1y vol / 5y correlation windows). Factor score is negative beta, cross-sectional z-scored so low-beta names rank highest, matching the long leg of the original long-short construction.

alphas.nickname: Carhart 1997 momentum — 12m-1m return
alphas.notes: Carhart (1997) UMD momentum factor. Return from 12 months ago to 1 month ago, so the most recent month is skipped and today's price never enters; cross-sectional z-score per date for long-short ranking. Top z-scores = winners. Constructed directly from prices, so this matches the original definition modulo the z-score wrapper. Canonical 252d window; declared decay_horizon=60 due to registry schema cap (le=60); real signal horizon=252.

alphas.nickname: [PRICE PROXY] FF2015 CMA — investment via inverse volume growth
alphas.notes: [PRICE PROXY] for the Fama-French (2015) CMA (Conservative Minus Aggressive) investment factor. The original definition uses total-asset growth from fundamental data; here we use the negative 60-day change in log average volume as an activity-growth proxy, then cross-sectional z-score per date for long-short ranking. Top z-scores = volume contraction (conservative / low-growth proxy).

alphas.nickname: correlation-rewiring stability score
alphas.notes: Causal rolling rendition of the correlation-regime skill's Mode 4 (rewiring leaderboard): per-asset row mean of |corr(event) - corr(calm)| where the event window is the trailing 20 bars and the calm baseline is the 120 bars immediately before it, sign-flipped and cross-sectionally z-scored so correlation-stable names rank highest. Framed as a structural risk / crowding lens, not a validated alpha: the author's public validation of the underlying regime machinery covers regime detection and attribution on historical replays only and makes no return-prediction claim for this cross-sectional form

alphas.nickname: George-Hwang 2004 52-week-high momentum
alphas.notes: George & Hwang (2004) 52-week-high momentum. Ratio of current close to the trailing 252-day maximum close, cross-sectional z-score per date for long-short ranking. Top z-scores = names trading nearest their 52-week high. Canonical 252d window; declared decay_horizon=60 due to registry schema cap (le=60); real signal horizon spans months.

alphas.nickname: [PRICE PROXY] FF1993 HML — value via inverse 252d return
alphas.notes: [PRICE PROXY] for the Fama-French (1993) HML (High Minus Low) value factor. The original definition uses book-to-market ratio from fundamental data; here we use the negative 252-day total return as a long-term reversal proxy, then cross-sectional z-score per date for long-short ranking. Top z-scores = long-term underperformers (deeper value). Canonical 252d window; declared decay_horizon=60 due to registry schema cap (le=60); real signal horizon=252.

alphas.nickname: Amihud 2002 illiquidity — |return| per dollar volume
alphas.notes: Amihud (2002) ILLIQ. Daily |simple return| divided by dollar volume (close * volume), averaged over a trailing 21-day window, then cross-sectional z-score per date for long-short ranking. Top z-scores = least liquid names, which carry the illiquidity premium. Uses a 1-day return (one extra warmup bar over the 21-day average window).

alphas.nickname: [PRICE PROXY] Market factor (Sharpe 1964) — 21d demeaned return
alphas.notes: [PRICE PROXY] for the Sharpe (1964) / Fama-French market factor (MKT-RF). The original definition uses value-weighted market excess returns; here we use a 21-day per-stock total return and cross-sectional z-score per date for long-short ranking. Top z-scores = strong recent winners; bottom = losers.

alphas.nickname: Harvey-Siddique 2000 return skewness — inverse 60d skew
alphas.notes: Harvey & Siddique (2000) skewness premium. Negative of the trailing 60-day sample skewness of daily simple returns, cross-sectional z-score per date for long-short ranking. Top z-scores = most negatively-skewed names, which command a return premium over lottery-like positively-skewed names. Uses a 1-day return (one extra warmup bar over the 60-day window).

alphas.nickname: [PRICE PROXY] FF2015 RMW — quality via inverse 60d volatility
alphas.notes: [PRICE PROXY] for the Fama-French (2015) RMW (Robust Minus Weak) profitability factor. The original definition uses operating profitability from fundamental data; here we use the negative of 60-day return volatility as a low-vol-quality proxy, then cross-sectional z-score per date for long-short ranking. Top z-scores = lower vol (quality / robust).

alphas.nickname: [PRICE PROXY] FF1993 SMB — small-minus-big via inverse dollar-volume
alphas.notes: [PRICE PROXY] for the Fama-French (1993) SMB (Small Minus Big) size factor. The original definition uses market capitalization from book equity data; here we use the negative log of 60-day average dollar volume (close * volume) as a liquidity-weighted size proxy, then cross-sectional z-score per date for long-short ranking. Top z-scores = smaller / less liquid names.

alphas.nickname: Jegadeesh 1990 short-term reversal — inverse 21d return
alphas.notes: Jegadeesh (1990) one-month reversal. Negative trailing 21-day return, cross-sectional z-score per date for long-short ranking. Top z-scores = recent one-month losers, which tend to rebound. Constructed directly from prices, matching the original definition modulo the z-score wrapper.

alphas.nickname: Accruals - inverse (NI-CFO)/TA, Sloan 1996
alphas.notes: Balance-sheet accrual proxy: high accruals indicate low earnings quality; sign inverted so high score = low accruals. PIT-safe from the fundamental panel; missing statements remain NaN and are excluded from that date's cross-section.

alphas.nickname: Asset growth - inverse investment factor
alphas.notes: Inverse PIT-safe asset-growth factor. High asset growth is treated as aggressive investment and receives lower scores; low/negative growth receives higher scores.

alphas.nickname: Book-to-market - equity over market cap (FF HML characteristic)
alphas.notes: Valuation proxy: close times weighted-average diluted shares is not reported market capitalization; adjusted closes can change the level. Fama-French (1993) HML-style book-to-market proxy built from PIT-safe total equity and shares diluted aligned to the daily close panel; the academic_hml factor in the academic zoo is only a price proxy. High B/M (cheap relative to book value) scores high. market_cap = close x shares_diluted is computed here in the factor file by design: _fundamental_schema.py lines 210-212 deliberately keep price-dependent value factors such as book_to_market out of DERIVED_

alphas.nickname: Cash to assets - balance-sheet cash ratio
alphas.notes: Balance-sheet cash ratio (cash and equivalents / total assets): high cash holdings signal defensive capacity and financial flexibility. Zero or missing total assets become NaN via safe division before cross-sectional z-scoring; PIT-safe from the filed-date-anchored fundamental panel.

alphas.nickname: CFO yield - operating cash flow over total assets
alphas.notes: Valuation proxy: close times weighted-average diluted shares is not reported market capitalization; adjusted closes can change the level. Cash-flow return on assets: the cash-backed counterpart of ROA, so accrual-heavy earnings score lower here. Zero or missing total assets become NaN via safe division before cross-sectional z-scoring; PIT-safe from the filed-date-anchored fundamental panel.

alphas.nickname: Dividend yield TTM - dv_ttm (daily market data)
alphas.notes: Trailing dividend yield from the val: namespace (tushare daily_basic dv_ttm, CN A-share only), reported in percent units — cross-sectional z-scoring is scale-invariant, so no unit conversion is applied. High dividend yield scores high. Keyed by trade_date, so PIT-safe by construction with no filing lag. Missing dates or non-CN symbols stay NaN and are excluded from that date's cross-section. Lineage: JoinQuant style-pro divyild; akshare/Eastmoney dv_ttm convention.

alphas.nickname: Dividend yield TTM industry-neutral - within-industry dv_ttm (daily market data)
alphas.notes: Industry-neutralized trailing dividend yield: each name is z-scored against its Shenwan level-1 industry peers instead of the whole cross-section (sector tag from tushare index_member_all SW2021 membership, point-in-time via in_date/out_date). This removes the industry confounding that dominates raw A-share dividend yield — mature banks and utilities pay structurally high dividends while growth industries pay almost none, so a raw high-yield screen is largely an industry bet. High dividend yield relative to industry peers scores high; dv_ttm is reported in percent units and cross-sectional z-s

alphas.nickname: Earnings growth - sign-safe YoY net income expansion
alphas.notes: PIT-safe earnings growth from the fundamental panel's derived field ``earnings_growth``. The schema-side formula is sign-safe: delta net_income / abs(lag_365d net_income), so a negative year-ago base does not flip the growth sign (the proposal #6 footnote resolution; the alternative NaN-on-negative-base was not chosen). Calendar-day lag per the #1564 lesson. High earnings growth scores high, matching the JoinQuant net_profit_growth_rate convention. Missing statements or a zero/missing year-ago base remain NaN and are excluded from that date's cross-section.

alphas.nickname: Earnings yield - net income over market cap
alphas.notes: Hybrid value factor using PIT-safe net income and shares diluted aligned to the daily close panel. Division by zero/non-finite market cap becomes NaN before cross-sectional scoring.

alphas.nickname: FCF yield - (CFO - capex) over market cap
alphas.notes: Valuation proxy: close times weighted-average diluted shares is not reported market capitalization; adjusted closes can change the level. PIT-safe free-cash-flow yield: FCF = CFO - capex, scaled by market cap (close x shares_diluted) computed in the factor file per the _fundamental_schema.py price-dependent convention. Sign assumption: capex is reported as a positive magnitude (SEC concept PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment), so subtracting it from CFO yields FCF directly. High FCF yield (cheap on cash generation, cf. Lakonishok-Shleifer-Vishny 1994 cash-flow yield value factors) score

alphas.nickname: Gross profitability - gross profit over total assets
alphas.notes: PIT-safe Novy-Marx style gross profitability from the fundamental panel; cross-sectional z-score per date with missing issuers excluded.

alphas.nickname: Leverage - inverse debt/equity (low leverage scores high)
alphas.notes: PIT-safe market leverage (total debt / total equity) from the fundamental panel; sign inverted so low leverage scores high — heavily levered firms carry distress risk and lower expected returns. Zero-equity or missing statements already yield NaN in the derived field and are excluded from that date's cross-section.

alphas.nickname: Operating margin - operating income over revenue
alphas.notes: Operating profitability (operating income / revenue), cross-sectionally z-scored per date. Captures pricing power and cost efficiency before financing and tax effects. Zero-revenue or missing statements become NaN via safe division and are excluded from that date's cross-section; PIT-safe from the fundamental panel.

alphas.nickname: P/B - inverse price-to-book (daily market data)
alphas.notes: Nonpositive multiples are excluded rather than ranked as cheap. Inverse price-to-book from the val: namespace (tushare daily_basic pb, CN A-share only): low PB (cheap relative to book value) scores high, the daily-market-data counterpart of fund_book_to_market. Keyed by trade_date, so PIT-safe by construction with no filing lag. Missing dates or non-CN symbols stay NaN and are excluded from that date's cross-section. Lineage: JoinQuant style book_to_price_ratio; akshare/Eastmoney pb convention.

alphas.nickname: P/B industry-neutral - inverse within-industry price-to-book (daily market data)
alphas.notes: Nonpositive multiples are excluded rather than ranked as cheap. Industry-neutralized inverse price-to-book: each name is z-scored against its Shenwan level-1 industry peers instead of the whole cross-section (sector tag from tushare index_member_all SW2021 membership, point-in-time via in_date/out_date). This removes the industry confounding that dominates raw A-share PB — banks and cyclicals are structurally cheap on book value while technology names are structurally expensive, so a raw low-PB screen is largely an industry bet. Low PB relative to industry peers scores high. A name with no ind

alphas.nickname: P/S TTM - inverse price-to-sales (daily market data)
alphas.notes: Nonpositive multiples are excluded rather than ranked as cheap. Inverse trailing price-to-sales from the val: namespace (tushare daily_basic ps_ttm, CN A-share only): low PS scores high. PS stays informative for loss-making names where earnings yield fails. Keyed by trade_date, so PIT-safe by construction with no filing lag. Missing dates or non-CN symbols stay NaN and are excluded from that date's cross-section. Lineage: JoinQuant style-pro sales-to-price; akshare/Eastmoney ps_ttm convention.

alphas.nickname: P/S TTM industry-neutral - inverse within-industry price-to-sales (daily market data)
alphas.notes: Nonpositive multiples are excluded rather than ranked as cheap. Industry-neutralized inverse trailing price-to-sales: each name is z-scored against its Shenwan level-1 industry peers instead of the whole cross-section (sector tag from tushare index_member_all SW2021 membership, point-in-time via in_date/out_date). This removes the industry confounding that dominates raw A-share PS — software and platform names carry structurally high margins and high PS while distributors and manufacturers are structurally low, so a raw low-PS screen is largely an industry bet. Low PS relative to industry peer

alphas.nickname: Revenue growth - YoY top-line expansion
alphas.notes: PIT-safe revenue growth from the fundamental panel's derived field ``revenue_growth`` (revenue / lag_365d(revenue) - 1, calendar-day lag per the #1564 lesson rather than a row-wise shift). High top-line growth scores high, matching the JoinQuant operating_revenue_growth_rate convention. Missing statements or a missing year-ago base remain NaN and are excluded from that date's cross-section.

alphas.nickname: ROA - return on assets (PIT-safe fundamentals)
alphas.notes: PIT-safe return on assets (net income / total assets) from the fundamental panel; cross-sectional z-score per date. Higher ROA means a more profitable asset base and scores higher. Missing statements remain NaN and are excluded from that date's cross-section.

alphas.nickname: ROE - return on equity (PIT-safe fundamentals)
alphas.notes: PIT-safe return on equity from the fundamental panel; cross-sectional z-score per date. Missing statements remain NaN and are excluded from that date's cross-section.
